Approximate Stokes viscosity

1. Data used
Bubble radius
—
Selected liquid density
—
Air density (kg/m³)
Terminal velocity
—

Radius and terminal velocity are converted to SI units using the current length calibration. Air density defaults to 1.225 kg/m³; edit it for your lab conditions.

2. Formula

μ = [2 r² (ρliquid − ρair) g] / (9 vt),   g = 9.81 m/s²

3. Substitution

Enter a calibrated radius and enough position points to estimate terminal velocity.

4. Result

—

A result requires a measured fluid density, calibrated bubble radius, and positive upward terminal velocity.

Set the origin by clicking the flask's bottom center. Plots show vertical distance and velocity relative to that point; upward is positive. Coordinates in the position log remain image-based.

Measurement uncertainties use independent instrument errors combined in quadrature: balance ±0.01 g, syringe ±0.01 mL, and ruler ±0.1 cm. Pixel clicks, frame rate, and air density are treated as exact. Ruler-scale uncertainty is shared by calibrated measurements.
